title: Replicating the Confident-Wrong Failure: Abstention Collapse Under Binary Scoring

original_idea.body: Replicating the Confident-Wrong Failure. Problem: the argument that hallucination is partly an artifact of binary scoring penalizing 'I don't know' is straightforward to demonstrate empirically on open models. Direction: on SimpleQA-style hard questions, prompt under standard vs abstain-if-unsure-no-penalty regimes, measure how confident-wrong rate, abstention, calibration shift; characterize how prompt framing reshapes the honesty/guessing tradeoff.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain but it's a demonstration of a known argument; catastrophic-risk link is a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Two-regime prompting on SimpleQA-style items; very accessible.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Largely confirms a known incentive argument; limited novel externally-doable slice.

novelty.reasoning: OpenAI's argument is published and abstention-prompting effects are known; largely confirmatory.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The binary-scoring/abstention argument is published; this empirically confirms a known claim.
